findings.title: Universal core offers "Save to file" in chat apps and never defines it
findings.issue: The menu line relies on the model knowing it can't write files ("drop this one if you can't write files"), and section 6 defines only Run it now and Refine. Picking Save to file therefore has no rules: no path, no never-overwrite. The acceptance criteria limit Save to file to Claude Code, and the docs promise it disappears in chat apps. The "Done ★" variant for media prompts appears only under "Run it now" in section 6, so the menu shows a confusing mix of the two. The MCP brief embeds this core verbatim (mcp/src/brief.ts:90-91, noted only for impact). File-capable MCP clients therefore get Save to file with none of the overwrite protection in SKILL.md:99.
findings.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:51 "3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)"; lines 55-58 have no Save rule. All four round-1 universal runs (claude -p with --tools '', recorded at 14:45-14:47, just before commit 124b72b; `git show 124b72b:universal/prompt-engine.md` has the same line 51) still end with "3) Save to file". Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-prompt-engine/d32a46dc-34ea-5901-8086-72e22db65686/scratchpad/universal-iter1/coding-standard-then-ok.turn2.md, writing-standard-then-override.turn2.md, writing-quick.turn1.md, midjourney-quick.turn1.md. The Midjourney run shows "1) Run it now ★ (I can't generate images, so I'd mark it "Done" and you'd paste it into Midjourney)". This contradicts docs/manual-checks.md:32 ("Save to file" should be missing, because chat apps can't write files) and universal/README.md:52 ("only appears in tools that can write files"). The test still reported 36/36 because it only checks for /What next\?/ (scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs:42).
findings.fix: Replace line 51 with: `- ### What next?: 1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine. Add 3) Save to file only if you have a tool that writes files on the user's computer; chat apps usually don't, so leave it out. Option 1 becomes "Fill placeholders ★" while [[placeholders]] remain, and "Done ★" plus where to paste it for an image or video prompt you can't generate.` Add to section 6: `- Save to file: save only the full prompt to prompts/<short-name>.md or the path the user gives; never overwrite an existing file (add -2, -3…); reply with the path.` This adds about 450 characters, so the core stays under 7,500 and keeps the contract string "Save to file". Then add a universal-test check that a tools-disabled menu contains no "Save to file".

findings.title: Secret handling sends the user back to paste the key again
findings.issue: SKILL.md:38 and universal:14 turn a pasted key into `[[api key]]`. Every placeholder goes under "Fill before running" (output-format.md:57). The menu then leads with "Fill placeholders ★" (output-format.md:75), and Run it now says "If placeholders are still open, ask for their values first" (SKILL.md:97; universal:56). Followed literally, the method asks the user to type the secret into the chat again. It never says to prefer an environment variable or to suggest rotating the exposed key. It also gives no place in the fixed template for that notice, so the model improvises.
findings.evidence: In both recorded runs of evals/secret-redaction-quick, the model ignored the placeholder rule and used OPENAI_API_KEY. The grader was then loosened, with a comment calling the env var "the better practice in a prompt for a coding agent" (evals/secret-redaction-quick/graders/02-key-replaced.md; docs/compatibility.md:45). In /tmp/claude-eval-MIHtOh/out/trace.jsonl the first line says "I replaced your API key with a placeholder" although it used an env var. It also inserts an off-template "**Security note:** … Consider rotating it" block between Score and What next, against SKILL.md:82 ("in this order and nothing else"). /tmp/claude-eval-laesm0/out/trace.jsonl puts the rotation advice under "Fill before running" instead.
findings.fix: Replace SKILL.md:38 with: `- **Secrets and private data.** Never copy API keys, passwords or tokens into the prompt. In prompts for code or agents, refer to an environment variable (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`); elsewhere use a placeholder such as `[[api key]]`. Replace other people's private details with placeholders. Say so in your first line and suggest rotating any key that was pasted. Never ask the user to type a secret's value, including for Fill before running or Run it now.` Mirror it in universal/prompt-engine.md:14. Add to the output-format.md "Fill before running" rule: "For a secret, say where to set it (an environment variable or the tool's secret settings), never ask for its value."

findings.title: Replies to the What next? menu are undefined, so ok or "Fill placeholders" can start a run
findings.issue: Users are taught that `ok`, `yes` or 👍 "accept every ★" (SKILL.md:66; questions.md:79; universal:33), and the menu stars "Run it now". Section 6 never says how to read ok, 👍 or "thanks" at the menu. Text menus are used in Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, Claude.ai and the universal prompt. There, an acknowledgement can be read as picking Run it now, which starts file edits for a coding prompt and breaks "nothing runs until the user picks". The "Fill placeholders ★" option replaces Run it now (output-format.md:75), but nothing defines what it does, and the universal core has no such option. The menu table has no precedence rule when rows overlap, for example open placeholders and a prompt meant for another tool.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:95-100 cover only Run it now, Refine, Save to file, and dismissal or silence. The model defines "Fill placeholders" on its own in /tmp/claude-eval-QL3hfk/out/trace.jsonl: "1. Fill placeholders ★: give me your company name, team details and anecdotes, and I'll run the prompt". So picking "fill" also runs the prompt. No eval case or manual check sends `ok` at the menu (this was not observed failing; it is untested).
findings.fix: Add to SKILL.md section 6, and as one line to universal section 6: `- Only an explicit choice counts: the option's number or name, or the dialog pick. Treat ok, 👍, thanks or praise as no choice: say the prompt is ready and wait. Fill placeholders asks for the values, shows the filled full prompt, then shows the menu again with Run it now ★; it runs nothing by itself.` Under the output-format.md table, add: "When several rows apply, use the first that fits: can't generate media → Done; placeholders open → Fill placeholders; another tool → Try it here." Mark questions.md:79 as "(question rounds only)".

findings.title: Specific values the model picks get tagged [best practice] and never appear under Assumptions
findings.issue: [best practice] is defined loosely ("something the method adds"). image-video.md:10 asks for "labelled defaults" without saying where the label goes, and SKILL.md:88 doesn't define the tag at all. Models therefore tag specific values they picked themselves (objects, counts, framing) as best practice and leave them out of Assumptions. The user can't see them as guesses or change them with "change N", which weakens the labelled-assumptions honesty rule.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-eval-yXOtsf/out/trace.jsonl (Midjourney, quick): "**Exact details: one lantern, a crescent moon, a stone chimney** [best practice]". The lantern and the moon appear in no Assumption. /tmp/claude-eval-i7jr1A/out/trace.jsonl: "針葉樹は三本、星空 [best practice]" (three conifers, starry sky) is missing from Assumptions, while "ミディアムワイドショット" (medium-wide shot) appears in both lists. evals/save-to-file/history.jsonl: "Alternative titles and tags [best practice]" and also Assumption 4. In the universal round-1 output writing-standard-then-override.turn2.md (before commit d63abbf), skipped ★ answers are tagged [best practice] and repeated as Assumptions 1-4, against universal:48-49.
findings.fix: Replace output-format.md:62 with: `- **[best practice]** — a kind of rule or section the method adds, such as success criteria or an uncertainty rule. The specific values you picked for it (three pines, a lantern, 3:2, 150–250 words, two alternative titles) are defaults: list them under Assumptions, not here.` Append to SKILL.md:88: "Specific values you picked yourself go under Assumptions, not [best practice]." Change image-video.md:10 to end "…add missing details only as defaults listed under Assumptions." Add the same clause to universal:48.

findings.title: A ★ can be a non-answer like "Tell me", which `ok` can't accept
findings.issue: The method promises that `ok`, or skipping a question, accepts every ★, but it never requires the ★ option to be usable as it stands. questions.md:29 also pushes toward artifact requests ("Paste the error message"), which can't be dialog questions because AskUserQuestion needs 2-4 options. If the ★ is a non-answer, an `ok` reply leaves that question unanswered, and the model has to guess or ask again.

Never star "tell me", "paste it" or "other". When only the user has the information (their stack, an error message, a voice sample), star a usable fallback such as "Let the agent detect it from the repo" or "Leave a [[placeholder]]", and ask for the artifact in one line after the questions.` Add to SKILL.md:57: "the ★ must work as an answer if the user replies ok".

findings.title: build.mjs does nothing, silently, when its path has a space, goes through a symlink, or is on Windows
findings.issue: The main-module guard compares import.meta.url with `file://${process.argv[1]}`. import.meta.url is percent-encoded, is the realpath of the file, and on Windows uses forward slashes; argv[1] is none of those. When they differ, main() never runs: `node scripts/build.mjs` writes nothing and `--check` exits 0 with no output, even on a stale tree. version.mjs:73 runs build.mjs this way, so a version bump can leave mcp/src/generated/content.ts with the old VERSION. On macOS, os.tmpdir() is under /var, which is a symlink to /private/var, so the first test in version.test.mjs fails there. validate.mjs then says "stale; run node scripts/build.mjs", but running that command does nothing.
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy at .../review-scratch/with space/repo, with media-targets.md made stale: `node scripts/build.mjs --check` gives exit 0 and no output; `node scripts/build.mjs` gives exit 0 and leaves the file unchanged; `node scripts/validate.mjs` reports "error: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs". Re-running against the current build.mjs, including the in-flight edit, gives the same result. With TMPDIR pointing at a symlink: `node --test scripts/test/version.test.mjs` gives "not ok 1 - sets the version everywhere and the repository still validates ... error: mcp/src/generated/content.ts: stale". I simulated macOS on Linux with that symlink. I did not run Windows; the failure follows from comparing "file://C:\..." with "file:///C:/...".

findings.title: The history sanitizer writes API keys, tokens, home paths, hostnames and session IDs into fixtures meant for a public repo
findings.issue: sanitize() keeps message, toolUseResult and thinking blocks word for word. It rewrites only the exact repo and cwd strings, and its only scan is an ASCII e-mail regex. Any other private data in a kept field is written to the fixture: the first message, assistant text and thinking, and any file the allowed Read tool opens. There are four more problems: (a) The path rewrite runs on serialized JSON, where Windows backslashes are escaped, so Windows paths are never rewritten. (b) The e-mail regex refuses ordinary package specs such as next-auth@5.0.0 without saying where the match is, yet misses non-ASCII addresses. (c) The transcript is looked for only in ~/.claude/projects, ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and only after the billed call. (d) Importing the module runs the recorder, so sanitize() has no tests. The three committed fixtures are clean today, and the type filter drops the attachment events that hold the account e-mail, so the risk is in future recordings.
findings.evidence: End to end, with a fake `claude` on PATH and a fake HOME (no model call), in .../review-scratch/probes/rh: the planted transcript has an sk-ant-api03-... key and a ghp_... token in the first message. A thinking block holds a /home/alice/... path, alice-mbp.corp.internal, the original session UUID and a claude.ai session_... URL. `node scripts/eval/record-history.mjs out.jsonl "..."` exits 0, and grep finds all six in out.jsonl. probes/sanitize-probe.mjs: "next-auth@5.0.0" and "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.2.3" are REFUSED as "e-mail-like string"; "jürgen@müller.de" is WRITTEN; Windows repo and cwd paths are WRITTEN unchanged. With CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set, claude is called once and then the script fails: "Error: transcript for session ... not found under .../.claude/projects". Importing the module prints the usage text and exits 2.
findings.fix:
(1) Put lines 19-57 under a realpath-based main guard, so sanitize() can be imported. Add scripts/test/record-history.test.mjs using the planted transcript.
(2) Before serializing, walk every string in the kept events and replace: repo with /plugin, cwd with /workspace, os.homedir() with ~, os.hostname() with <host>, and the original sessionId with FIXED_SESSION. Drop message.id. Rewriting the parsed strings also fixes Windows paths.
(3) After serializing, refuse to write, printing "line N: <kind>", if any of these match:
/\bsk-ant-[\w-]{20,}/
/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/
/\b(?:gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}|github_pat_\w{20,})/
/\bxox[abprs]-[\w-]{10,}/
/\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/
/\beyJ[\w-]{10,}\.[\w-]{10,}\./
/-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/
/(?:\/(?:Users|home)\/[^/\s"\\]+|[A-Za-z]:\\\\Users\\\\)/
/\bsession_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/
and, for e-mails, /[\p{L}\p{N}._%+-]+@[\p{L}\p{N}-]+(?:\.[\p{L}\p{N}-]+)*\.\p{L}{2,}/u (the top-level domain must be letters, so pkg@1.2.3 passes). In probes/secret-scan.mjs these patterns find nothing in the three committed fixtures and catch every planted item.
(4) Read transcripts from join(process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(homedir(), '.claude'), 'projects').

findings.title: refreshHistory finds the skill body by guesswork, which can corrupt or freeze the recorded skill text without failing any check
findings.issue:
The body is taken from the first "\n# " to lastIndexOf('ARGUMENTS:'). That breaks in three ways:
(a) Claude Code appends an ARGUMENTS line only when there are arguments, and SKILL.md:34 itself contains `ARGUMENTS:`. For a recording made without arguments, the end point lands inside the old body, so the new body is spliced in front of the stale rest of the old one. The result doesn't change on later builds, so build --check and validate pass.
(b) Any text before SKILL.md's H1 is duplicated on every build. build --check never passes again, and validate keeps saying "stale".
(c) If the body has no H1, start is 0 and the refresh is skipped from then on, silently.
In all three cases the follow-up evals test something other than the current SKILL.md.
findings.evidence:
Claude Code 2.1.312 bundle: `if(!ke&&r&&n)e=e+"\n\nARGUMENTS: ${w(n)}"`, so the line is added only when there are arguments.
Case (a), probes/refresh-noargs.mjs (a recording without arguments, whose old body differs in its last line): "expected length 10026 | got 18266 ... stale \"(OLD RULE)\" still present: true ... second build changes it again: false".

findings.title: refreshHistory leaves stale file copies in toolUseResult and turns partial reads into whole files
findings.issue: For each refreshed Read, only the tool_result text is replaced. The same event's toolUseResult.file (content, numLines, totalLines) keeps the recorded copy, so the committed fixtures already hold two versions of output-format.md. A Read with offset/limit is replaced by the whole file, numbered from 1. A Read of a file that no longer exists is left stale, with no warning.
findings.evidence: In evals/followup-ok-accepts-recommendations/history.jsonl and evals/followup-partial-answers/history.jsonl, the toolUseResult.file.content for references/output-format.md differs from the current file at lines 61 and 64: it still has the old "[your answer]" rule, without "including ★ recommendations they accepted". Y=W?.file?.content`), but I could not confirm from the minified code how resume uses it. probes/refresh-partial.mjs: a Read with offset 4 and limit 2 is refreshed to all 10 lines plus an extra "11\t" line, and its toolUseResult is unchanged.

findings.title: The universal prompt's behavior test passes outputs that break the contract, and its runs depend on the developer's own config
findings.issue:
Three checks are too loose:
- 'ok reply line' is /\bok\b/i, so any "OK" passes even when the "Reply `ok` to accept every ★" line is missing.
- 'what next menu' looks only for "What next?", not for the Run it now ★ and Refine options the user asked for.
- 'no full prompt yet' misses a full prompt written under a bold label instead of a heading.
The runs pass only --system-prompt and --tools ''. According to `claude --help` (2.1.312), --tools covers "the built-in set", and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery, hooks and MCP servers are turned off only by --bare, --safe-mode or --strict-mcp-config, none of which are passed. So results vary with the developer's ~/.claude setup.
findings.evidence:
probes/universal-checks.mjs, with the checks copied unchanged:
- "questions, no reply line" (ends "It is OK to skip any question."): every check PASSES.
- "questions + full prompt in bold": "PASS no full prompt yet".
- "menu without options" ("### What next?\nLet me know."): all 7 STRUCTURE checks PASS.
Help text: --tools "Specify the list of available tools from the built-in set"; --bare skips "hooks ... auto-memory ... and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery"; --safe-mode starts with "CLAUDE.md, skills, installed plugins, hooks, MCP servers ... disabled".
findings.fix:
Change the checks to:
['ok reply line', has(/Reply\s+`?ok`?\s+to accept every ★/i)]
['what next menu', has(/What next\?[\s\S]*Run it now[^\n]*★[\s\S]*Refine/i)]
['no full prompt yet', (t) => !/(#+\s*|\*\*)Full prompt/i.test(t)]
Better still, read the strings from data/contract.json. Add '--safe-mode' and '--strict-mcp-config' to the args at line 26; both are listed in claude --help 2.1.312. Check the tool list in one run's init output to confirm the isolation.

findings.title: Re-running a release fails before npm and the MCP Registry, so a failed publish can't be finished from CI
findings.issue: Only the npm step (lines 45-48) checks whether its target already has this version. `gh release create` aborts when the tag's release already exists, and the MCP Registry rejects a version it already has. GitHub re-runs every step of a failed job. So if anything after the GitHub release step fails (expired or wrongly scoped NPM_TOKEN, registry outage while it is in preview, a network error), every re-run stops at 'Create the GitHub release' and never reaches npm or the registry again. A re-run after a full success also fails at the registry step. docs/publishing.md:62 describes only the skip paths, not recovery.
findings.evidence: gh CLI v2.89.0 pkg/cmd/release/create/create.go:499-506. When assets are passed (as here) it calls publishedReleaseExists and returns `a release with the same tag name already exists: <tag>`. Registry v1.8.6 internal/service/registry_service.go:279-281 returns ErrInvalidVersion, which internal/database/database.go:19 defines as "invalid version: cannot publish duplicate version". cmd/publisher/commands/publish.go returns that as an error, so the step exits non-zero.
findings.fix: Guard both steps the way the npm step is guarded. (1) GitHub release: `if gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "Release ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} already exists; skipping"; else gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" $prerelease --generate-notes dist/prompt-engine.zip dist/prompt-engine.mcpb dist/prompt-engine.md dist/prompt-engine-knowledge.md dist/SHA256SUMS; fi`. gh publishes the release only after every asset has uploaded, so an existing published release already has them. (2) Registry, before downloading the publisher: `enc="$(node -p 'encodeURIComponent(require("./server.json").name)')"; if curl -fsS -o /dev/null "https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/${enc}/versions/${version}"; then echo "already in the MCP Registry"; exit 0; fi`. I checked this endpoint today: it returns 200 for a listed version (ac.inference.sh%2Fmcp/versions/1.0.0) and 404 for io.github.vipul-goel%2Fprompt-engine/versions/0.1.0. (3) Add to publishing.md step 6: "If a run fails, fix the cause and re-run it; each step skips what is already published."

findings.title: The only CI path to npm (NPM_TOKEN) is scheduled to stop working in January 2027, and the trusted-publishing alternative needs a newer npm than Node 22 bundles
findings.issue: The npm step publishes with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN taken from the NPM_TOKEN secret, and publishing.md:21 recommends that setup. npm's docs say direct publishing with granular access tokens will be removed in January 2027, about two months from now. The replacement npm recommends, trusted publishing (OIDC), needs npm CLI 11.5.1 or later, but `node-version: 22` installs npm 10.9.x, so publishing.md:22's 'small changes' include a newer npm. publishing.md:21 also doesn't say which token options CI needs. 'Bypass 2FA' is off by default, and when it's off, account- and package-level 2FA settings apply to publishing.
findings.evidence: npm/documentation at commit 514e6c9 (2026-10-29): about-access-tokens.mdx:82 says "The ability to publish new package versions directly with a granular access token will be removed in **January 2027**". about-access-tokens.mdx:45 says Bypass 2FA "is set to false by default at token creation". trusted-publishers.mdx:9 says it "requires npm CLI version 11.5.1 or later and Node version 22.14.0 or higher". trusted-publishers.mdx:50 says "The workflow file must exist in `.github/workflows/`". trusted-publishers.mdx:232 says a new configuration must complete its first publish within 2 days. trusted-publishers.mdx:266 says provenance is automatic. nodejs.org/dist/index.json, checked today: v22.23.4 bundles npm 10.9.9; v24.22.2 bundles npm 11.19.1. The January 2027 date is npm's stated plan and may move, so recheck it before relying on it.
findings.fix: Move the npm publish to trusted publishing. In that step or job: `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version: 24` and `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`; remove `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` and the empty-token branch; keep the `npm view` skip; run `npm publish --access public`, which generates provenance automatically. Keep `id-token: write`. On npmjs.com, after the first manual publish (trusted publishers are set up on the package's settings page, trusted-publishers.mdx:37), add a GitHub Actions trusted publisher: owner vipul-goel, repository prompt-engine, workflow `release.yml`. Then push the tag within 2 days. Update release.yml:4 and publishing.md:12, 19-22, 62 and 93 to match. If you keep a token until then, publishing.md:21 should say it must be a granular token with 'Read and write (publish and stage)' and 'Bypass 2FA', limited to prompt-engine-mcp once the package exists, and that npm plans to stop accepting it in January 2027.

findings.title: Every step of the single release job gets contents: write and id-token: write, including third-party code
findings.issue: Permissions are set at the workflow level, and everything runs in one job. That includes: `npm ci`, whose lockfile has install scripts for @modelcontextprotocol/inspector 2.13.0 and esbuild 0.28.2; the TypeScript/vitest test suite; the esbuild bundler; release.mjs; and `npm publish`, whose prepublishOnly hook (mcp/package.json:47) re-runs `npm run build && npm test` with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN in its environment. A downloaded binary runs in the same job too. actions/checkout keeps the write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN available to later steps by default. Any step can also request an OIDC token, and the registry turns a github-oidc login into publish rights over every server under io.github.vipul-goel/*, not just this one.
findings.evidence: release.yml:9-11 grants `contents: write` and `id-token: write` to the whole workflow, and release.yml:17 doesn't set persist-credentials. actions/checkout v7 README:33: "The auth token is persisted in the local git config ... Set `persist-credentials: false` to opt-out." Registry v1.8.6 internal/api/handlers/v0/auth/github_oidc.go:293: `ResourcePattern: fmt.Sprintf("io.github.%s/*", claims.RepositoryOwner)`. The registry's docs (github-actions.mdx, 'Securing your registry token in CI') warn that such a token can publish and overwrite any server in the namespace. mcp/package-lock.json: hasInstallScript is set for @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.13.0, esbuild@0.28.2 and fsevents.
findings.fix: Set `permissions: {}` at the top and split the work into jobs. (1) `build` with `contents: read`: checkout with `persist-credentials: false`; `npm ci`, build and test in mcp/; `node scripts/release.mjs --tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`; `npm pack --pack-destination ../dist` in mcp/ after the build; upload `dist/` with actions/upload-artifact@v7. (2) `github-release` (needs build) with `contents: write`: actions/download-artifact@v7, then `gh release create` with `GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` and no checkout. (3) `npm` (needs build) with `contents: read, id-token: write`: download the artifact and run `npm publish dist/prompt-engine-mcp-*.tgz --provenance --access public --ignore-scripts`. The tarball from `npm pack` already includes LICENSE, so no lifecycle scripts need to run. (4) `registry` (needs npm) with `contents: read, id-token: write`: checkout with `persist-credentials: false` for server.json, then the verified publisher. Optionally gate the publish jobs with a protected `environment:` limited to v* tags. Update publishing.md:24 to describe the per-job permissions.

findings.title: The mcp-publisher binary is downloaded and run without any checksum or signature check, contrary to the registry's own instructions
findings.issue: `curl ... | tar xz mcp-publisher` extracts the release asset and runs it straight away in a job that can mint OIDC tokens and holds a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN. Pinning v1.8.6 doesn't protect the asset, because release assets can be replaced. The registry's GitHub Actions guide for this exact flow says to verify the download first.
findings.evidence: modelcontextprotocol/registry at tag v1.8.6, docs/modelcontextprotocol-io/github-actions.mdx:14-17: "The examples pin `mcp-publisher` to a specific release and verify its Sigstore bundle before extracting it." Its example (lines 64-83) runs `cosign verify-blob`. Today the v1.8.6 asset mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz has SHA-256 1fbe93fc0783c2394d8012c8d6e50a59e98cb2cc2d216264cc69f405d0e21340. That matches line 5 of the release's registry_1.8.6_checksums.txt, and the .sigstore.json bundle exists.
findings.fix: Replace line 67 with: `archive=mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz; curl -fsSL -o "$archive" "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/download/v1.8.6/$archive"; echo "1fbe93fc0783c2394d8012c8d6e50a59e98cb2cc2d216264cc69f405d0e21340  $archive" | sha256sum -c -; tar xzf "$archive" mcp-publisher`. Alternatively, copy the docs' block: sigstore/cosign-installer pinned by SHA, then `cosign verify-blob --bundle "$archive.sigstore.json" --certificate-identity https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v1.8.6 --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com "$archive"`. Update the hash whenever the version pin changes.

findings.title: Opens a new, identical issue every month (and on every manual run) while entries stay stale
findings.issue: The step runs `gh issue create` whenever anything is stale. It never looks for last month's open issue, so a reminder nobody has handled gets a new twin each month, and each workflow_dispatch adds another. All 12 entries share last_verified 2026-10-29, so they go stale together.
findings.evidence: verify-data.yml:37-39 calls `gh issue create --title "Re-verify image/video tool data"` with no lookup. I replayed the step's logic (60-day cutoff) against data/media-targets.json at the cron times (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-prompt-engine/d32a46dc-34ea-5901-8086-72e22db65686/scratchpad/scripts/stale_sim.mjs). 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-03 have 0 stale entries. 2027-01-03, 2027-02-03 and 2027-03-03 each have 12, which means three identical issues unless every entry is fixed in between.
findings.fix: Replace the step body with: `[ -s stale.md ] || exit 0; title="Re-verify image/video tool data"; { echo "These image and video tool entries ..."; echo; cat stale.md; } > body.md; existing="$(gh issue list --state open --search "\"$title\" in:title" --json number,title --jq ".[] | select(.title == \"$title\") | .number" | head -n1)"; if [ -n "$existing" ]; then gh issue edit "$existing" --body-file body.md; gh issue comment "$existing" --body "Still stale on $(date -u +%F)."; else gh issue create --title "$title" --body-file body.md; fi`. The existing `issues: write` permission covers list, edit and comment. Change publishing.md:98 to say it opens or updates one issue.

findings.title: Dispatch inputs are pasted straight into the shell script, and the API key is exposed to the CLI install
findings.issue: `${{ inputs.runs }}` and `${{ inputs.max_cost_usd }}` are expanded into the script text before bash runs it, in a step whose environment holds ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. A value such as `1" ; <command> ; echo "` runs arbitrary commands. The inputs have no type, so typos also pass unchecked. The impact is limited: only users with write access can dispatch, and GitHub notes they can already read the repository's secrets. Still, this is the pattern GitHub documents as script injection. Separately, the key is in the environment of `npm install -g`, whose postinstall (`node install.cjs`) doesn't need it.
findings.evidence: evals.yml:32: `--runs "${{ inputs.runs }}" --max-cost-usd "${{ inputs.max_cost_usd }}"`. findings.issue: GitHub Actions only runs workflow files from .github/workflows/. All four workflows are committed under .github/pending-workflows/.
